greet: Ah, {name}, what a fine coat! Let me guess, Tulan wool? No? Pity, I'd have sold you the lot.
Well met, {name}! Tell me, do you know what madder fetches this side of the pass?
{name}! I was just saying to the fire, that is a face with money in it.
Evening, {name}, sit, sit, you look like a man who appreciates a bargain.
Hello there, {name}! Cheap wool, dear dye, and the best company in the Inn, all at once.
Ho, {name}, I'd know that cloak anywhere, or at least I'd know its cousin in Verdan.
Good evening, {name}! Between us, I've had a dreadful week and a splendid one, both at once.
Ah, {name}! Come here, feel this sleeve. Feel that? Finest weave on the mountain.
{name}, you've a shrewd look. I trust you, which is more than I say to most of this room.
accept: Gladly! I was hoping someone would ask, I'm half broke from waiting for the right company.
Of course, of course! Nothing like a bit of sport to warm up the cold bones of a trader.
Aye, I'm yours for the evening. Let's make it a splendid one before the barkeep shuts us out.
Yes indeed. I'd trade my best mule for a chance like this, and you know I'd be sorry to.
Certainly, {name}, I'm delighted. Shall we say the usual terms, or shall we invent new ones?
decline: Ah, not tonight, {name}, I've a ledger to balance and my sums want quiet.
No, no, that's too rich a risk for my purse, I'm afraid. Another time, perhaps.
Sorry, {name}, I'd love to, but the wind has been sharp and I'm mindful of my coin.
Thanks kindly, {name}, but I've made a rule to decline anything before I've had a proper look.
I'd rather not, {name}. Too many eyes in this room, and I can't count them all at once.
No thank you, {name}. I'll keep my money in my boot where it belongs, safe and sound.
I must pass, {name}, sorry. My feet are wanting rest and my mind is wanting a better offer.
Not for me this evening, {name}. Ask me again when the price has dropped a little.
Kindly no, {name}. I'm a trader, not a fool, and you've a glint in your eye I don't trust.
pressed: Forgive me, I'll be back presently. Keep an eye on my cloth, it's worth more than my life.
I have to go, I'm afraid. Don't let anyone buy my chair while I'm away!
Pardon, I need a moment away from the table. Mind the cups, I'll not be long.
Give me a breath, I must go. My business waits, and so does my patience, which is thinner.
Sorry, I'm off for a moment. Keep my place warm, won't you? I'll be back to finish our talk.
Would you excuse me? I shall return. Everyone hold their wagers until then.
Pardon, I'm going out for a bit. Don't wager on the weather while I'm gone, I'd only lose.
Right, I must step away. Keep my seat, and if anyone asks, I'm counting my profits.
Excuse me, I need to go. Back in a trice, friend, and then we'll see who wins.
content: That's me done for now, friend. A pleasure, truly, but I'm off to find better company.
Well, I've said my piece and sold my stock of talk for the evening. Good night to you.
I've had my fill of the fire and the dice tonight. I'll leave you to your own business.
Enough chatter for one night, I think. I'll take my leave while the deal is still sweet.
I've spent my words, and I'm wanting some quiet to count my profits. Fare you well.
That's all my patter for tonight, so I shall go and rest my tongue a while.
I'll be off now, before I talk myself into buying something I don't need.
My purse is light and my voice is hoarse, so I think I'll call it done for now.
Right, I've had my fill of company. You'll forgive me if I go and sit somewhere new.
I've made my rounds and sold what I could. I'll leave you in peace, friend.
closing: Last call, is it? Well, good night to you all, and may your coin always be heavy.
Closing time already? Then I'm off, good night, and mind the cobbles on the way out.
The barkeep's shutting up, so good night to all, and my thanks for the company.
That's the bell for bed. Good night, friends, and I'll see you when the road brings me back.
Time to go, I'm afraid. Good night to everyone, and no hard feelings about the wagers.
Off to bed with me, then. Good night, and may the next season bring better prices.
Shutters closing, is it? Good night, friends, and sleep well on your coin.
That's me, then. Good night to the room, and a safe road to whoever's walking home tonight.
Well, the fire's dying and so am I. Good night, all, and thank you for the fine evening.
Good night, the lot of you! I'll be counting my profits by the road tomorrow.
